key_insight: Jointly designing interpolant schedules and ODE discretizations yields condition-number-aware elliptic schedules and Zoloflow, a Gaussian sampler with minimax-optimal score-query complexity.
engineering_relevance: Accounting explicitly for target conditioning can make probability-flow sampling more efficient while providing rigorous error guarantees for Gaussian and log-concave targets.
method: Use complexified ODE trajectory analyticity to guide joint schedule and discretization design.
Derive variance-preserving schedules via conformal mapping and Jacobi elliptic functions, recovering the trigonometric schedule as κ approaches 1.
Pair elliptic schedules with a tailored discretization linked to Zolotarev optimal rational approximants.
evidence_signal: The abstract proves Gaussian minimax optimality among oblivious score-span algorithms and log-concave Wasserstein guarantees, and reports evaluations on synthetic and image-generation benchmarks without numerical results.
watch_item: Gaussian optimality assumes exact score queries; practical performance depends on score approximation quality and specifying the target condition number κ.
paper_title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
